literal: Of right conduct those who renounced [their] greatness, as excellence, desires [to declare] the scriptures' conclusion.
translation: The greatness of those who stand in right conduct and have renounced all desires is the supreme truth that scriptures desire to proclaim above all else.
modern: ஒழுக்க நெறியில் நின்று ஆசைகளைத் துறந்தவர்களின் பெருமையையே, சிறந்ததாக நூல்களின் துணிவு போற்ற விரும்புகிறது.
explanation: This couplet extols the greatness of those who have renounced worldly desires while firmly adhering to the path of righteous conduct. The word 'nīttār' refers to those who have renounced self-centered desires, while 'olukkam' emphasizes that their renunciation is rooted in moral discipline. The term 'panuval' refers to sacred texts or scriptures, and 'tuṇivu' means their ultimate, settled conclusion. The poet states that the ultimate consensus of all wise scriptures is to hold the greatness of these self-controlled ascetics as the highest virtue worth praising.
